Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  November 3, 2022

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on
November 3, 2022, via Zoom. Commissioner Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:00
p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Jacob
  Fragoso - District 2, Commissioner Cynthia McLemore - District 3,
  Commissioner Christopher Beck - District 4, Commissioner Henry
  Brown - Commissioner at Large
  Absent:  None

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Sabrina Barnes  Parks, Recreation, and Community Services Director
  Anthony Harris  Recreation Supervisor
  Bharat Devlia  Food Services Manager
  Craig Civitello  Lead Park Maintenance Worker
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. Minutes for July 7, 2022, were tabled until the next meeting.

STAFF REPORTS.

SUMMER FOOD SERVICE AND CHILD AND ADULT CARE FOOD PROGRAMS. Staff report
dated November 3, 2022, recommending the Park and Recreation recommend the Mayor
and Council Members approve an agreement between the City of Inglewood and
Freshlunches, Inc., dba Unity Meals in the amount of $345,670 for the provision of
breakfast, lunch, and snacks for the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) and
Summer Food Service Program (SFSP) from November 28, 2022, through August 31, 2023.
(CDE Grant Fund)

It was moved by Commissioner McLemore and seconded by Commissioner Fragoso that
the Commission hereby approves the recommendation. The motion was carried by the
following roll call vote:

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

Ayes: Commissioners Brown, Fragoso, McLemore, and Denmon
Noes: None.

AGREEMENT WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY REGIONAL PARK AND OPEN SPACE DISTRICT
FOR TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAM SERVICES. Staff report dated November 3,
2022, was presented recommending the Park and Recreation Commission recommend
the Mayor and Council Members take the following actions: A. Adopt a resolution to
amend the Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Budget to reflect the award of a Technical Assistance
Program grant in the amount of $285,000; and B. Approve a master agreement between
the City of Inglewood and Los Angeles County Regional Park and Open Space District
(RPOSD) for Technical Assistance Program Services. (Grant Fund)

It was moved by Commissioner Brown and seconded by Commissioner McLemore that
the Commission hereby approves the recommendation. The motion was carried by the
following roll call vote:

Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore, Brown, and Denmon
Noes: None.

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORTS - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. The Lead Park Maintenance Worker, Craig Civitello
reported that the Parks Division has begun preparation for the installation of the Dream
Fields at Edward Vincent, Jr. Park, coordinating with the Los Angeles Dodgers and working
closely with their contractors. Graffiti Abatement has removed graffiti from the water
plant reservoir on Crenshaw located in District 1. The team is still busy in District 4 around
the intersections of Dixon near Prairie and Crenshaw off 104th Street. They have also been
busy in District 3 from La Cienega Boulevard to La Brea.

REPORTS - RECREATION. Recreation Supervisor, Anthony Harris, reported the City of
Inglewood and the Los Angeles Rams are proud to present a flag football league to benefit
the youth. The 2022 Inglewood Rams flag football season began with a flair on September
25, 2022, as 10 of our Prep Division participants (Ages 11 through 12) made an
appearance on the NFL Game Day morning show at SoFi Stadium with Hall of Famers Kurt
Warner, Michael Irvin, former NFL head coach Steve Mariucci, and host Rich Eisen. The
league is filled with 17 teams over 4 age groups and totaling 225 participants. Teams
practice once a week for one hour and play games on Thursday evenings and Saturdays.
The league last 10 weeks and concludes on December 17, 2022 with team banquets for
all teams. There will be food, fun, and awards for participants. The City of Inglewood will
host its 8th Annual Turkey Giveaway Presented by Pepsi on Tuesday, November 22, 2022,
from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. at Hollywood Park. The Thanksgiving Turkey Giveaway is a drive-

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

thru event and participants must be registered in advance. To register, call the Parks,
Recreation, and Community Services Department at (310) 412-8750. The city's Annual
Holiday Tree Lighting Ceremony will be held Thursday, December 1, 2022, at 6:00 p.m.
There will be live entertainment, refreshments, and a special visit from SANTA!

REPORTS - HUMAN SERVICES. The Food Services Manager, Bharat Devlia reported the
Nutrition Program serves approximately 300 seniors per week and continues in
collaboration with the Social Justice Institute to provide fresh produce weekly. We
continue to provide home-delivered meals to homebound seniors and congregate
lunches at our Senior Center. Our lunchroom is set up to accommodate safe social
distancing and we look forward to continuing to provide freshly cooked meals daily to our
seniors. The Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) is tentatively scheduled to start
on November 28, 2022, at four locations (Rogers Park, Darby Park, Crenshaw Library, and
Main Library). Our Senior and Disabled Paratransit service continues to provide trips to
critical appointments such as dialysis and doctors' appointments. Drivers as well as
passengers continue to wear facemasks coverings. We have also been scheduling seniors
and persons with disabilities to other next-day requested appointments with no major
issues to report. The Senior Center is steadily getting back into the swing of things by
adding more classes and activities so that seniors can start to get back to enjoying their
senior center. Our most popular class by far is our chair exercise class. Two of our most
recent addition to classes are the Ethiopian Community ESL class as well as the
conversational Spanish class.

REPORTS - DIRECTOR. The Director of Parks, Recreation, and Community Services,
Sabrina Barnes reported on Capital Improvement updates: A. Vincent Park renovation
between the Dodgers Foundation and the City of Inglewood baseball fields is scheduled
to be completed by May 2023. B. The pump track project has stalled due to the
stabilization and packing of the storm drain-related issues. A full update will be provided
during our next scheduled meeting C. Restroom construction project has received its last
and final inspection with a two-month completion date. The project was stalled due to
permit issues. D. Mr. Devlia has assisted with grant funding for our playgrounds. The goal
is to make Edward Vincent, Jr. Park look brand new. E. Darby Park's Restroom project is
underway awaiting insurance documents . F. A budget has been approved for an
additional restroom at Edward Vincent, Jr. Park funded by Community Development
Department, the restroom is located near the Willie Agee Playhouse. It is expected to
start as the current project is finishing up. G. Additional funding were received for
playground surfacing with a focus on the Dennis the Menace playground that has buckled
and to start design work for new office space for Park staff, an engaging consultant has
submitted their proposal. H. An initial request for money to pave and or paint all parking
lots and surfaces at our parks was made and although not fully funded a small allocation
was received. We are working with Public Works employee, Hunter Nguyen to thermal

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

restripe the parking area at Champions Field. Updates will be provided as other projects
become on deck.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner McLemore asked when the city closes for
the holidays. Director Barnes stated on December 16, 2022, reopening on January 3,
2023. Some programs such as the Senior Center work through the Holidays.
Commissioner Beck thanked the staff for their reports. Commissioner Denmon stated the
plant-related classes held at Darby Park were excellent.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:32 p.m.
